name: Videographer
seoDescription: Videographers pay about $270/yr for General Liability, $450 with E&O. Learn how drone flights, gear on location, and post-production disputes affect cover.

industryContext.contextNote: Videographers carry expensive camera and audio equipment to varied filming locations, giving them equipment and premises-liability exposure similar to photographers but with more gear.

riskFactors.title: Equipment Theft or Damage
riskFactors.description: Cameras, drones, lighting, and audio gear are high-value and frequently transported, increasing loss and damage exposure.

riskFactors.title: On-Location Property Damage
riskFactors.description: Setting up lighting rigs, tripods, or drones at a client's venue can accidentally damage property or injure bystanders.

riskFactors.title: Post-Production Delivery Disputes
riskFactors.description: Lost footage, missed deadlines, or edits that don't match client expectations can trigger contract disputes, especially for one-time events.

faqs.question: Why do videographers need Commercial Property or gear coverage?
faqs.answer: This coverage protects expensive camera, lighting, and audio equipment against theft or damage while being transported or used on location, which most standard policies exclude.

faqs.question: What is the average cost of business insurance for a videographer?
faqs.answer: A videographer in the $0-50k revenue tier pays an estimated $270 per year for baseline General Liability coverage.

faqs.question: Does a videographer flying a drone need extra coverage?
faqs.answer: Drone operation for commercial video work often requires separate aviation liability coverage, since standard General Liability policies typically exclude aircraft-related claims.

faqs.question: Do venues require videographers to carry insurance?
faqs.answer: Many wedding venues and event spaces require a Certificate of Insurance showing General Liability coverage before allowing a videographer to film on-site.

blogContent.whyThisRiskFactor: Videographers carry a 1.05 actuarial risk factor, reflecting equipment and on-location liability slightly above still photographers due to more extensive gear.
blogContent.howCalculated: Premiums scale with revenue tier, team size, and Commercial Property/Gear or Errors & Omissions endorsements.
blogContent.comparisonNote: Videographer premiums are slightly higher than freelance photographers, reflecting the greater equipment value typically involved in video production.
